fits.wls: prespecified weighted-log fit of ln[1 - 2P(n)], primary for the X-memory decision
fits.binomial: binomial maximum-likelihood refit of all round counts (App. stats)

per_placement.method: observed: inverse-variance mean over the five days, se widened by sqrt(chi2/nu) when chi2/nu > 1 (nu = 4); binomial sigmas are half-widths of the quasi-likelihood 68% profile intervals. observed_plain: plain mean over the five days, se = sd / sqrt(5). predicted: plain mean over the five days of the model's prediction (each job's measured f), fitted with the same estimator. ratio = observed_plain / predicted_mean, so both sides are averaged alike; its se carries the observed error only. Lambda is pooled from the daily ratios (inverse-variance). The t test is within one placement (nu = 4); there is no test across placements.

placements_compared.note: No estimate, p-value or bound across placements is given: on every day these were the only usable distance-5 placements, and they overlap.

prespecified.source: runs/combined.json (pooled_x), the prespecified code at v0.2.0
prespecified.note: Record only (appendix): the rule treats the ten repetitions as independent.

agreement_tests.source: docs/analysis/results/fits.json (agreement, agreement_tests); wls replicates runs/combined.json model

calibration_scatter_check_exploratory.label: exploratory; the added spread comes from the predictions only (calibrations and idle-test f)

selection_check (reported errors on the.what: chosen day's mean reported error / mean over the other four days, per patch; mean over the five days

tracking.what: placement 1, Lambda_X: its prediction barely depends on f, so the predicted day-to-day swing comes from the calibration alone

prejob.what: predictions stored before each job (prediction.json) at f = 0 and f = 1, fitted like the data. The observed eps are decoded with priors at the job's measured f.

table_one_convention.convention: every cell, observed and predicted: plain mean over the five days. Observed error sqrt(sum sigma_i^2) / 5, multiplied by sqrt(chi2/nu) when chi2/nu > 1, chi2 about the plain mean, nu = 4. sigma_i is each estimator's own sampling error: binomial, half the 68% quasi-likelihood profile interval; WL, the delta-method sigma as prespecified in X memory, and in Z memory, where that sigma is unreliable near P = 1/2 (see errors), the parametric-bootstrap sd of the WL estimator. Predicted: plain mean of the daily predictions fitted the same way, with their range.

errors.what: ratios are bootstrap sd / quoted sigma: above 1, the quoted sigma is too small. Parametric bootstrap, 2,000 replicates per curve drawn from its binomial fit (fits.json).

window.note: WL tests refitted from results/fits_counts.json exactly as prespecified, f term from the frozen f = 0 and f = 1 predictions refitted in the same window. Binomial O/M: point estimates, both sides fitted alike; Student t interval over the ten repetitions.

selection.what: excess per round O - M in percentage points and the factor O/M, per patch (plain mean or geometric mean over the five days, t 4 dof). An equal additive excess gives a larger factor at the smaller eps, so only the additive scale and the fixed-against-reselected comparison speak to selection.

xy_variance_correction.what: old: Var(ln r) = (1 - r^2)/(N r^2) as prespecified (run.py:1059); new: delta method for separately sampled <X> and <Y>, Var(ln r) = [x^2(1-x^2)/N_X + y^2(1-y^2)/N_Y]/r^4 (with the (1+1/N) shot-noise factors).

downstream.source: results/idle_f_{compare,reanalysis,reanalysis_control,combined_fixed,combined_control}.json; control = unpatched rerun in the same environment

largest_observed_Lambda_X_change.note: observed values move because the decoder weights depend on f

heating_exploratory.what: Fractional change of each error rate from the start (t=0) to the end (t=1) of a job's shots; slope of the series-normalized rate against time. See heating.py docstring.

onset_line.note: two CZ counts only (relays 3, flags 8): the line joins the two roles' means

beta_gamma_dd_on_gamma_phi.what: OLS slope of ln Gamma_dd on ln Gamma_phi over physical qubits (per-qubit medians); 1 if one f fits every qubit, 0 if Gamma_dd ignores IBM's T2

per_qubit_f_decoding.basis: X (Z memory is unchanged in every job)

fit.model: Delta(l) = A r^l + C, l = 1..7 rounds, unweighted least squares on the mean over series
